name: Neo-brutalism
summary: A loud, friendly register: flat saturated colour blocks on a lavender canvas, 3 px ink outlines on every surface, hard zero-blur offset shadows in ink, sunflower-yellow panel heads and accent with ink text, chunky 900-weight display type and buttons that press down into their shadow. Playful, legible, never soft.
use_when: opt-in only: the brief names neo-brutalism, neo-brutalist, neubrutalism or the Korean 네오브루탈리즘
consumer, creator, community or education products that want energy and personality
launch pages, pricing pages and onboarding that should feel bold and hand-made rather than corporate
avoid_when: regulated, clinical, financial or enterprise tones
very dense data screens where outlines on every cell would turn into noise (keep tables quiet inside one outlined wrap)
the brief asks for brutalism without neo (that is computational-brutalism)
signature: thick ink outlines: 3 px on surfaces, 2 px on controls, the same ink in light and dark
hard offset shadows with zero blur (6 px on surfaces, 3 px on controls) in ink; this is the recorded neo-brutalist register CF-403 accepts
buttons press into their shadow on :active (translate 3 px, shadow to 0)
flat saturated fills: panel heads are solid yellow bars with ink text; ui-panel--accent, ui-panel--accent-2 (electric blue) and ui-panel--support colour the featured blocks
chunky type: 900-weight display with tight leading, 800-weight headings and figures, sentence case
tilted ui-sticker labels as the accent art, never over body text
bouncy but short motion (overshoot ease, 100–280 ms)
forbid: blurred, soft or coloured drop shadows (DS-007: the lock declares offset elevation)
thin grey borders on surfaces (outlines are ink)
more than four accent hue families in one view
rotated body text, or a sticker covering text
outlines and shadows on every table cell or list row
